Aker conducted a brief optimization study to estimate the amount of energy that could be saved at T-RICH if its customer(s) is able to send CO via pipeline at pressures higher than 15 bar. 2 The design is currently based upon gaseous CO arriving from a local distribution system at 15 barg and 2 up to 38°C / 100°F. This concept requires three stages of compression with intercooling to liquefy the product. The advantage of a gaseous pipeline is that for inlet pressures below approximately 30 bar there is no risk of liquid drop out in the pipeline upstream of T-RICH. Gas pipeline networks operating at higher pressures have a greater risk of liquid formation during low temperatures but may reduce compression load in the liquefaction plant. Long and medium distance CO pipelines typically operate in the Dense Phase to avoid liquid formation 2 within the network (above the critical pressure no separate liquid phase is produced at the range of normal ambient temperatures), with pressures let down at the inlet to the plant. Pipeline diameters can be reduced due to compressed fluid under transport. During expansion CO will drop below the critical 2 pressure and cool meaning that liquids may be formed and must be handled within the process. Depending on the expansion pressure CO can be routed to different stages of the process to capture 2 liquid and compress gas efficiently. High arrival pressure can reduce plant complexity and cost but requires a dense phase pipeline network to be installed upstream of T-RICH. Such a pipeline network is required to transport CO over longer 2 distances. By operating a dense phase pipeline network with an arrival pressure at T-RICH of 85barg or above, the following savings can be realized  Replace LP, MP and HP Stages of Compression with smaller LP, MP and HP Recycle Compression  Reduce peak power consumption by ~40%  Estimated cost saving: $10M per year in electricity costs plus equipment cost savings This optimization option is able to achieve significant savings because by significantly raising the incoming pressure, the Low and Medium Pressure compression stages can be eliminated, and the CO is instead 2 directed to the High Pressure flash drum upstream of the stripper column to recover liquids generated during the expansion process. As a result, two new recycle compressor stages are required to move gas from LP & Flash Drums to the HP Compressor Suction.
